hypotheses.claim: N, S and D can each parse the complete current G9 V3 plus Dialect corpus under a production-like deterministic LALR design after the same structural and lexical-identity repairs.
hypotheses.falsifier: Normative parser integration exposes a current admitted construct that one candidate cannot map to the intended typed IR without a semantic escape hatch.

hypotheses.claim: Reserved-keyword exclusion from generic NAME plus explicit keyword-identifier aliases removes observed lexical ambiguity while preserving reconstructible keyword-field identity and BOOLEAN identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production parser/canonicalizer finds a current legal identifier that cannot be represented or a keyword alias whose canonical identity differs across roundtrip.

hypotheses.claim: Finite declared bare relation words are currently the best source-surface candidate because they minimize migration edits while retaining fail-closed typed relation resolution and competitive parse cost.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: N or S yields lower target-reader repair cost, smaller maintenance burden or safer compiler evolution despite higher current migration cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched target-reader/compiler/Ubuntu tests show D materially worse on repair accuracy, semantic mistakes, parser maintenance, latency or evolution cost.

hypotheses.claim: The remaining high-information N/S/D discriminator is target-reader plus normative compiler integration rather than more local parser closure testing.
hypotheses.falsifier: A new local executable counterexample differentiates N/S/D on semantic correctness before target-reader execution.
